title: If The Elevator Ever Stops On A Floor That Doesn't Exist… DO NOT STEP OUT

lines.text: If the elevator ever stops on a floor that doesn't exist... do not step out.
This file is intended for employees who work after standard hours.
It contains seven rules. Please follow them in order.
The Bureau is not responsible for outcomes resulting from rules followed out of order.
Rule one. Know how many floors your building has.
Count them. Write the number down. Keep it in your wallet.
You will need it when the panel disagrees with you.
Rule two. If the elevator stops and the display shows a number not on your list, remain inside.
The doors will open. This is normal.
The hallway will look like your hallway. This is also normal.
Do not confirm it.
Rule three. Do not press the door close button.
The button is connected to nothing on this floor.
Pressing it tells the floor you are in a hurry.
Floors remember who is in a hurry.
Rule four. If someone on the floor says your name, do not answer.
Bureau records show that in one hundred percent of cases, the voice was correct about the name.
In zero percent of cases was it a coworker.
Answering is considered acceptance of a position on that floor.
Rule five. The doors will close on their own in approximately ninety seconds.
It will feel longer. Count to ninety out loud.
If you reach one hundred, begin again from one.
Do not skip numbers.
It notices.
Rule six. When the elevator moves again, do not look at the display.
It may show your floor. It may show a floor with letters. Press nothing.
Exit only when the doors open onto a hallway with a fire extinguisher.
The extra floor has never bothered to install one.
Rule seven. If you followed rules one through six, and you are reading this file at your desk...
check your floor directory again.
Count them.
Write the new number down.
Keep it in your wallet.
End of file.
Further training materials are available.
